response: # Audit of `apps/geometry-cathedral.html` (current main) I read the whole file and did not run it. The patches below are untested, and the numbers come from the code, not from a device. ## 1. Why sliders feel dead on iPhone 1. **Debounce starvation (line 121).** `clearTimeout(refreshTimer); refreshTimer=setTimeout(build,50)` restarts on every `input` event. iOS fires `input` about every 16 ms while you drag, so a structural slider rebuilds nothing until you stop for 50 ms. Nothing changes during the drag, and it all pops at release. 2. **Dead-by-omission sliders.** `resonance` is not in `structural` (line 118). In Cathedral and Torus it only changes its label until some other slider triggers a rebuild. 3. **The "animation" is almost nothing.** `advance()` (line 116) only transforms the whole root group. - Rotation is `0.048 rad/s × speed`, about 1.3°/s at the default. - Pulse is `±4% × pulse` scale. - Drift rotates `rotation.z` by at most about 0.04 rad. - Particles, filaments and pearls never move individually. - `fieldFrequency` is described as "Moving luminous wave", but no wave exists. It only sets the frequency of that 4% scale pulse. 4. **Control mode hides the feedback response.** - The plant output only drives `root.scale = 1 + x·0.14`. A target change of 0.5 gives about 7% scale. - The loop is closed, so after about 2 s it settles and the gain sliders show nothing. - The controller only resets on `build()`, so moving a gain does not replay a transient. - `disturbance` is rejected by the loop and moves the scale by less than 1%. - There is no plot, only a number updated every 140 ms. 5. **Quality slider half-dead on phones (line 113).** On mobile with bloom on, the pixel ratio clamps to 1.25. On a DPR-3 phone, `1.6·q/1.3` already hits that at q≈1.02, so quality 1.0–2.0 does nothing. 6. **Layout.** The sticky stage is 63 svh, so only about a third of the screen is left for sliders. The range input is 3 px tall with an unstyled track. The thumb is 22 px, which is a poor touch target. ## 2. same | Layout | | quality | ◐ (on phones, 1.0–2.0 clamped) | same | same | same | Perf | Straight talk on math versus cosmetics: - **Real math:** the Control PID/ODE, and the Flamm height `2√(rs(r−rs))` in Gravity (exact at warp = 1). - **Artistic parametric curves, not physics:** Cathedral and Torus. Gravity particles are static decoration, not geodesics. - **Cosmetic:** everything else, including pulse, drift and fieldFrequency, which are root transforms. - **Mislabeled:** the "Moving luminous wave" hint and "Core radiance". ## 3. Patches Together these give you: - mode-aware controls that are hidden when they don't apply (P1); - no starved rebuilds (P2); - a real shader-driven motion layer for the dynamics sliders (P3); - live material, hue and particle-count updates (P4); - a PID kick, a target step, a plot and a change badge (P5); - iPhone-friendly sliders and constants (P6). ### P1. Hide mode-irrelevant controls In `buildControls`, add `field.dataset.key=key;` right after `field.className='field';`. Then add: ```js const ALL=['cathedral','torus','gravity','control'], CTK=['cathedral','torus','control']; const SCOPE={branches:CTK,layers:CTK,symmetry:CTK,radius:CTK,twist:CTK,chaos:['cathedral'],pearls:['cathedral'], filament:CTK,innerGlow:CTK,metallic:CTK,mass:['gravity'],warp:['gravity'],grid:['gravity'], kp:['control'],ki:['control'],kd:['control'],setpoint:['control'],damping:['control'],disturbance:['control']}; function applyVisibility(){ $$('.field').forEach(f=>f.hidden=!(SCOPE[f.dataset.key]||ALL).includes(mode)); $$('details.group').forEach(d=>d.hidden=![...d.querySelectorAll('.field')].some(f=>!f.hidden)); $('#controlCount').textContent=$$('.field:not([hidden])').length+' CONTROLS'; } ``` - Call `applyVisibility()` at the top of `setMode` and once before the final `build()` in the init line. - CSS: `[hidden]{display:none!important}@media(min-width:801px){.field[data-key=stageHeight]{display:none}}` - `pearls` stays Cathedral-only unless you also make Torus and Control generate `params.pearls` pearls. ### P2. Throttle rebuilds and keep PID state Replace the structural and hue branches of `updateImmediate` with `requestBuild()`: ```js let bq=false,lastB=0; function requestBuild(){ if(bq)return; bq=true; setTimeout(()=>{bq=false;lastB=performance.now();build()},Math.max(0,120-(performance.now()-lastB))); } ``` This is leading and trailing, so the scene changes about 8 times per second during a drag. - Add `'resonance'` to `structural`. Gate it with `if(key==='resonance'&&(mode==='gravity'||mode==='control'))` so it does not rebuild there. In Control it is a live disturbance frequency. - Remove `controller={...};physicsAccum=0` from `clear()`. Put it in `setMode()` instead, so dragging a structural slider does not restart the PID. - `grid` still needs a rebuild. All the others below are handled live in P3 and P4. ### P3. Real motion: one shared vertex hook This drives lines, tubes, pearls, particles and the Flamm surface from GPU uniforms. There is zero rebuild and no per-frame CPU geometry work. ```js const U={t:{value:0},amp:{value:0},f:{value:3},k:{value:3},sw:{value:0}}; function anim(mat){ mat.onBeforeCompile=s=>{ s.uniforms.uT=U.t;s.uniforms.uAmp=U.amp;s.uniforms.uF=U.f;s.uniforms.uK=U.k;s.uniforms.uSw=U.sw; s.vertexShader='uniform float uT,uAmp,uF,uK,uSw;\n'+s.vertexShader.replace('#include ',`#include float s_=1.;vec3 p_=position; #ifdef USE_INSTANCING s_=length(instanceMatrix[0].xyz);p_=instanceMatrix[3].xyz; #endif float r_=length(p_.xz); float an_=uSw*.45*sin(uT*.7-r_*.5); vec3 q_=vec3(cos(an_)*p_.x-sin(an_)*p_.z,p_.y,sin(an_)*p_.x+cos(an_)*p_.z); vec3 d_=q_-p_; d_.y+=uAmp*sin(uK*r_-uT*uF+p_.y*1.7); d_.xz+=normalize(p_.xz+vec2(1e-4))*uAmp*.5*sin(uK*p_.y+uT*uF*1.3); transformed+=d_/s_;`);}; return mat; } ``` Wrap the materials with `anim(...)`: - `glowMat`: `return anim(new THREE.LineBasicMaterial(...))` - the `filament` MeshPhongMaterial - the `spheres` pearlMat - the `energyPoints` PointsMaterial - the gravity surface MeshPhongMaterial The twist is bounded (a sinusoid), so geometry never shears into a tangle. Do not use an unbounded `uT*swirl`. In `advance()`, after `t+=simDt`: ```js U.t.value=t; U.amp.value=params.pulse*.45; // pulse=0 → exact Flamm surface / undeformed shapes U.f.value=params.fieldFrequency; U.k.value=params.resonance; U.sw.value=params.drift; root.rotation.y+=simDt*.07; // was .048 (total ≈.12 rad/s at ×1) ``` This makes speed, pulse, drift, resonance and fieldFrequency visibly move filaments, pearls and particles in all four modes. They should then be shown in all modes, which is the default in P1. Shells: they are untouched by the shader, so wobble them. In `torusSurface`, add `animated.push({o:m,rx:m.rotation.x,f:.4+Math.random()*.6})`. In `advance`, add `for(const a of animated)a.o.rotation.x=a.rx+Math.sin(t*a.f)*(.05+params.pulse*.3);`. In Gravity the ripple is decorative. With pulse = 0 the surface is the exact Flamm paraboloid. Say so in the hint. ### P4. Live updates with no rebuild **Particles.** Build `PMAX=950` points once and use the draw range. - In all four builders, change `i{const m=o.material,u=m&&m.userData;if(!u)return; if(u.shellK!=null)m.opacity=u.shellK*params.shell+(u.shellB||0); if(u.pearl){m.metalness=.15+params.metallic*.85;m.roughness=.5-params.metallic*.42;m.emissiveIntensity=params.innerGlow*.35} if(u.fil)m.emissiveIntensity=params.innerGlow*.8;})} ``` **Hue, live.** Remove `+params.hue/360` from `colorAt`, so build colors are the base palette. Then: ```js function applyHue(){const h=params.hue/360,c=new THREE.Color(),hs={}; const sh=col=>{col.getHSL(hs,THREE.SRGBColorSpace);col.setHSL((hs.h+h+2)%1,hs.s,hs.l,THREE.SRGBColorSpace)}; const arr=(a,k)=>{k.o??=a.slice();const b=k.o;for(let i=0;i{ if(o.isInstancedMesh&&o.instanceColor){arr(o.instanceColor.array,o.userData);o.instanceColor.needsUpdate=true} const ca=o.isPoints&&o.geometry.attributes.color;if(ca){arr(ca.array,o.userData);ca.needsUpdate=true} for(const m of [].concat(o.material||[])){m.userData.b??={c:m.color.clone(),e:m.emissive&&m.emissive.clone()}; m.color.copy(m.userData.b.c);sh(m.color);if(m.userData.b.e){m.emissive.copy(m.userData.b.e);sh(m.emissive)}}});} ``` Call it for `hue` and at the end of `build()`. Hue now also shifts fixed-colour shells and the Gravity surface, which it didn't before. **Stars.** In `createStars`, use `new THREE.PointsMaterial({size:1.8,sizeAttenuation:false,fog:false,opacity:.85,color:0xbfd6ea,transparent:true,depthWrite:false})`. ### P5. Control organism: make gain changes obvious, plus a plot In `advance`, replace the control branch's use of `params.setpoint`: ```js const sp=clamp(params.setpoint+(Math.floor(t/4)%2?-.4:.4),-1,1.2); // real reference step every 4 sim-seconds const e=sp-controller.x; /* …rest unchanged… */ hist.push(sp,controller.x,e); if(hist.length>3*240)hist.splice(0,3); let pulse=1+controller.x*.32+Math.sin(t*2)*params.pulse*.045; // was .14 U.amp.value=params.pulse*.45+Math.abs(e)*.35; // error visibly agitates geometry ``` Add `const hist=[];`. Add a kick, so a gain change replays the transient immediately: ```js let lastKick=0; function kick(){const n=performance.now();if(n-lastKick<250)return;lastKick=n;controller.x-=.7;controller.I=0;controller.v=0} ``` Call `kick()` from `updateImmediate` for `kp, ki, kd, damping, disturbance, setpoint`. Raise the disturbance term in `a` to `params.disturbance*2.5*Math.sin(…)` so it shows even with the loop closed. Plot: add `` inside `#stage`. ```js const pc=$('#plot').getContext('2d'); function drawPlot(){const cv=pc.canvas;cv.style.display=mode==='control'?'block':'none';if(mode!=='control')return; pc.clearRect(0,0,200,72);const n=hist.length/3; [[0,'#e4c99b'],[1,'#7dece2'],[2,'#ff7a8a']].forEach(([k,col])=>{pc.strokeStyle=col;pc.beginPath(); for(let i=0;i` in the stage. - At the top of `updateImmediate(key)`: ```js const kind=(structural.has(key)&&!['shell','metallic','innerGlow','particles'].includes(key))||key==='resonance'&&['cathedral','torus'].includes(mode)?'REBUILD':'LIVE'; $('#fb').textContent=`${key} = ${params[key]} · ${kind}`; ``` ### P6. iPhone usability and constants ```css .field input[type=range]{height:34px;background:none;margin:0;-webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent} .field input[type=range]::-webkit-slider-runnable-track{height:4px;border-radius:4px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#397d8d,#8bd9c9)} .field input[type=range]::-webkit-slider-thumb{width:28px;height:28px;margin-top:-12px} ``` - Set `:root --scene-height:46svh` and `initial.stageHeight:46`, so the scene and sliders are both visible. - `draw()`: replace the ratio lines with `const ratio=clamp(params.quality,.6,Math.min(devicePixelRatio||1,2));`. Change the quality slider to `.6–2`, labelled "Render scale (capped by device)". Every slider position now works. - Lower the default `bloom` to about 0.8 on phones, or keep it. It is live, and the quality-versus-bloom clamp is gone. - `autoRotateSpeed` 0.28 gives about a 3.5-minute revolution. Raise it to about 1.2 so "Auto-rotate" is noticeable. - The Focus mode hides the panel, so you can't tweak sliders there. That is fine, but a user on a phone may expect otherwise. ## 4. What this gives you Result per slider after the patches: - **Live, no rebuild:** speed, pulse, drift, resonance (motion), fieldFrequency, particles, hue, shell, metallic, innerGlow, bloom, exposure, stars, quality, and all PID gains (with a kick and the plot). - **Throttled rebuild at about 8 Hz:** branches, layers, symmetry, radius, twist, chaos, pearls, filament, mass, warp, grid. - **Hidden when irrelevant:** about 20 sliders per mode instead of all 32. Dead ones are no longer shown. The caveat I'd test first is the shader hook. If `normal`-dependent shading looks off on tubes at high pulse, lower the 0.45 multiplier. A real-device check on Safari is needed, since I couldn't run it here.
